details: Mixture-of-Agents, a methodology that enhances LLM capabilities by layering and aggregating outputs from multiple diverse models.

explainer.lead: Mixture-of-Agents (MoA) is a methodology that enhances LLM capabilities by layering and aggregating outputs from multiple diverse models. It matters because it can improve answer quality without training a new single larger model.

tiers.eli5: Instead of asking one expert, you ask several different experts and then combine their answers into one better answer.
tiers.practitioner: Engineers implement MoA as a pipeline where several models produce candidate responses that later layers review and merge into a final output. The pitfall is cost and latency, since every answer runs through many model calls.
tiers.paperLevel: Layered aggregation across diverse models: outputs from one layer are combined and passed to the next, with a final aggregator producing the response. Its limits are the added compute and latency of multiple model passes per query.

explainer.example: A query might first be answered by several different models, then a subsequent layer reads all those drafts and synthesises a single refined answer.
